checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the KZG batch verification pairing equation correctly implemented to prevent forged proofs?

reachability.notes: Batch verification is the primary cryptographic gatekeeper. An attacker submits cells, commitments, and proofs for verification. Any error in the verification equation allows forged data to be accepted.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_impl (SG-015) implementation. 2. Verify the pairing equation e(LL, LR) == e(RL, [1]) is correctly computed where LL = g1_lincomb(proofs, r_powers), LR = KZG_SETUP_G2_MONOMIAL[n], and RL = RLC - RLI + RLP. 3. Verify g1_lincomb correctly computes the linear combination of proofs with random powers. 4. Verify RLC, RLI, and RLP are computed correctly from commitments, interpolated values, and proof points. 5. Attempt to craft proofs with incorrect data that might pass verification due to edge cases. 6. Test with empty batches, single-element batches, and maximum-size batches. 7. Verify that ALL cells in the batch must pass - no partial acceptance.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0024, Trust Boundaries: tb-005, tb-006, tb-007, Invariant: SG-015-INV-001/005

checklist.title: Verify g1_lincomb computation in batch verifier produces correct linear combination of proofs

reachability.notes: Batch verification is the primary cryptographic gatekeeper. An attacker submits cells, commitments, and proofs for verification. Any error in the verification equation allows forged data to be accepted.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the g1_lincomb function used to compute LL = g1_lincomb(proofs, r_powers). 2. Verify r_powers are generated from a secure random source (Fiat-Shamir or similar). 3. Verify the linear combination arithmetic is correct for G1 point addition and scalar multiplication. 4. Test with known test vectors to confirm correctness. 5. Check for off-by-one errors in indexing proofs and r_powers. 6. Verify overflow/underflow protection in scalar operations.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0024, Supporting check for LL computation in pairing equation

checklist.title: Verify RLC, RLI, RLP components are correctly computed for the pairing equation right-hand side

reachability.notes: Batch verification is the primary cryptographic gatekeeper. An attacker submits cells, commitments, and proofs for verification. Any error in the verification equation allows forged data to be accepted.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Trace computation of RLC (commitment linear combination). 2. Trace computation of RLI (interpolation component). 3. Trace computation of RLP (proof-related component). 4. Verify RL = RLC - RLI + RLP arithmetic is performed in correct order and with correct field arithmetic. 5. Check for sign errors or missing negations. 6. Verify point subtraction is implemented correctly. 7. Test edge cases: zero commitments, identity points, points at infinity.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0024, Supporting check for RL computation in pairing equation

checklist.title: Verify KZG_SETUP_G2_MONOMIAL[n] trusted setup value is correctly selected and used

reachability.notes: Batch verification is the primary cryptographic gatekeeper. An attacker submits cells, commitments, and proofs for verification. Any error in the verification equation allows forged data to be accepted.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Verify the correct index 'n' is used when accessing KZG_SETUP_G2_MONOMIAL. 2. Confirm the trusted setup values match the expected ceremony output. 3. Check for off-by-one errors in index calculation for LR. 4. Verify the G2 point is validated before use (not point at infinity, on curve). 5. Ensure trusted setup is loaded from a trusted source and integrity-checked.

checklist.title: Verify pairing check returns True only when ALL cells in batch pass verification

reachability.notes: Batch verification is the primary cryptographic gatekeeper. An attacker submits cells, commitments, and proofs for verification. Any error in the verification equation allows forged data to be accepted.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Test batch with all valid proofs - should return True. 2. Test batch with one invalid proof among valid ones - MUST return False. 3. Test batch with all invalid proofs - should return False. 4. Verify no early-exit logic could cause partial verification. 5. Verify randomness in batch combination prevents an attacker from crafting proofs that cancel out errors. 6. Check that verification result is not inverted or mishandled in calling code.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0024, Critical: Must reject entire batch if ANY cell fails

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are commitment_indices validated for bounds and uniqueness before batch KZG proof verification?

reachability.notes: An attacker could submit out-of-bounds commitment_indices to cause array index out-of-bounds access, or duplicate commitments to manipulate the weight aggregation.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_impl function and locate where commitment_indices is processed. 2. Review if bounds checking exists: verify that commitment_indices[k] < len(commitments) for all k before any array access. 3. Review if duplicate detection exists: verify that commitment_indices contains no duplicate values before weight aggregation. 4. Craft a malicious P2P message with commitment_indices containing out-of-bounds values (e.g., index >= len(commitments)) and verify the implementation rejects it before array access. 5. Craft a malicious P2P message with duplicate commitment_indices values and verify the implementation either rejects duplicates or handles them safely without affecting the random linear combination's soundness. 6. Verify that rejection happens early (fail-fast) rather than after partial processing that could leak information or cause inconsistent state.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0025, Trust Boundary: tb-007, Invariant Reference: SG-015-INV-003/004. Out-of-bounds commitment_indices would cause a crash (DoS). Duplicate commitments could cause incorrect weight aggregation in the random linear combination, potentially allowing invalid proofs to pass.

checklist.title: Falsification Test: Can out-of-bounds commitment_indices bypass validation and cause array index out-of-bounds access?

reachability.notes: An attacker could submit out-of-bounds commitment_indices to cause array index out-of-bounds access, or duplicate commitments to manipulate the weight aggregation.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Construct a test case where commitment_indices contains an index equal to len(commitments) (off-by-one). 2. Construct a test case where commitment_indices contains a very large index value (e.g., MAX_UINT64). 3. Construct a test case where commitment_indices contains negative values (if the type allows signed integers). 4. For each test case, invoke verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_impl and verify: (a) No panic/crash occurs, (b) The function returns an appropriate error before accessing commitments array, (c) No partial state modification occurs.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0025, Pre-condition validation for commitment_indices bounds. This is a DoS vector if bounds checking is missing.

checklist.title: Falsification Test: Can duplicate commitment_indices manipulate weight aggregation in random linear combination?

reachability.notes: An attacker could submit out-of-bounds commitment_indices to cause array index out-of-bounds access, or duplicate commitments to manipulate the weight aggregation.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Understand the weight aggregation algorithm used in the random linear combination for batch verification. 2. Construct a test case with duplicate commitment_indices (e.g., [0, 0, 1] instead of [0, 1, 2]). 3. Analyze whether duplicates cause: (a) A commitment to be weighted multiple times, (b) Incorrect aggregation that could allow an invalid proof to verify as valid. 4. If duplicates are allowed by design, verify the mathematical soundness is preserved. 5. If duplicates should be rejected, verify rejection occurs before any cryptographic operations.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0025, Pre-condition validation for commitment_indices uniqueness. Duplicate handling affects the soundness of batch verification.
